'''Samir Mitragotri''' (born 28 May 1971) is an [[Indian American]] professor at [[Harvard University]], an inventor, an entrepreneur, and a researcher in the fields of [[drug delivery]] and [[biomaterials]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mitragotri Laboratory|url=https://drugdelivery.seas.harvard.edu/|website=Drug Delivery|publisher=The President and Fellows of Harvard College|accessdate=22 April 2018}}</ref> He is currently the Hiller Professor of Bioengineering and [[Hansjörg Wyss]] Professor of Biologically Inspired Engineering at [[Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences]] and the [[Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Renowned bioengineer to join Harvard faculty|url=https://www.seas.harvard.edu/news/2017/01/renowned-bioengineer-to-join-harvard-faculty|website=Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences|publisher=President and Fellows of Harvard College|accessdate=24 January 2017}}</ref> Prior to 2017, he was the Duncan and Suzanne Mellichamp Chair Professor at [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Endowed Chairs|url=http://www.ia.ucsb.edu/dev/endow.shtml|website=UCSB Institutional Advancement, Office of Development|publisher=The Regents of the University of California|accessdate=14 October 2014}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web|title=People |url=http://bioengineering.ucsb.edu/people |publisher=UCSB Center for BioEngineering, [[Regents of the University of California]] |access-date=2023-06-09 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141017031719/http://bioengineering.ucsb.edu/people |archive-date=October 17, 2014}}</ref>

Mitragotri has invented many novel drug delivery technologies, especially in the fields of transdermal, oral and targeted systems. He invented techniques to deliver drugs transdermally using low-frequency ultrasound,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Mitragotri|first1=S.|last2=Blankschtein|first2=D.|last3=Langer|first3=R.|title=Ultrasound-mediated transdermal protein delivery|journal=Science|date=11 August 1995|volume=269|issue=5225|pages=850–853|doi=10.1126/science.7638603|pmid=7638603|bibcode=1995Sci...269..850M|s2cid=26069484}}</ref> pulsed microjet injector,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Arora|first1=A.|last2=Hakim|first2=I.|last3=Baxter|first3=J.|last4=Rathnasingham|first4=R.|last5=Srinivasan|first5=R.|last6=Fletcher|first6=D. A.|last7=Mitragotri|first7=S.|title=Needle-free delivery of macromolecules across the skin by nanoliter-volume pulsed microjets|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date=6 March 2007|volume=104|issue=11|pages=4255–4260|doi=10.1073/pnas.0700182104|pmid=17360511|pmc=1838589|bibcode=2007PNAS..104.4255A|doi-access=free}}</ref> high throughput skin experimentation,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Karande|first1=Pankaj|last2=Jain|first2=Amit|last3=Mitragotri|first3=Samir|title=Discovery of transdermal penetration enhancers by high-throughput screening|journal=Nature Biotechnology|date=4 January 2004|volume=22|issue=2|pages=192–197|doi=10.1038/nbt928|pmid=14704682|s2cid=20478007}}</ref> skin penetrating peptides<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Hsu|first1=T.|last2=Mitragotri|first2=S.|title=Delivery of siRNA and other macromolecules into skin and cells using a peptide enhancer|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date=8 September 2011|volume=108|issue=38|pages=15816–15821|doi=10.1073/pnas.1016152108|pmid=21903933|pmc=3179050|bibcode=2011PNAS..10815816H|doi-access=free}}</ref> and ionic liquids.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Zakrewsky|first1=Michael|last2=Lovejoy|first2=Katherine S.|last3=Kern|first3=Theresa L.|last4=Miller|first4=Tarryn E.|last5=Le|first5=Vivian|last6=Nagy|first6=Amber|last7=Goumas|first7=Andrew M.|last8=Iyer|first8=Rashi S.|last9=Del Sesto|first9=Rico E.|last10=Koppisch|first10=Andrew T.|last11=Fox|first11=David T.|last12=Mitragotri|first12=Samir|title=Ionic liquids as a class of materials for transdermal delivery and pathogen neutralization|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date=16 September 2014|volume=111|issue=37|pages=13313–13318|doi=10.1073/pnas.1403995111|pmid=25157174|pmc=4169946|bibcode=2014PNAS..11113313Z|doi-access=free}}</ref> He also invented intestinal patches and ionic liquids for oral delivery of proteins.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Banerjee|first1=Amrita|last2=Ibsen|first2=Kelly|last3=Brown|first3=Tyler|last4=Chen|first4=Renwei|last5=Agatemor|first5=Christian|last6=Mitragotri|first6=Samir|date=25 June 2018|title=Ionic liquids for oral insulin delivery|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=115|issue=28|pages=7296–7301|doi=10.1073/pnas.1722338115|issn=0027-8424|pmc=6048483|pmid=29941553|bibcode=2018PNAS..115.7296B|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Whitehead |first1=Kathryn |author-link=Kathryn Whitehead |last2=Shen |first2=Zancong |last3=Mitragotri |first3=Samir |date=23 July 2004 |title=Oral delivery of macromolecules using intestinal nanoparticles that hitch a ride on red blood cells, monocytes and other circulatory cells for tissue-specific delivery.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Anselmo|first1=Aaron C.|last2=Gupta|first2=Vivek|last3=Zern|first3=Blaine J.|last4=Pan|first4=Daniel|last5=Zakrewsky|first5=Michael|last6=Muzykantov|first6=Vladimir|last7=Mitragotri|first7=Samir|title=Delivering Nanoparticles to Lungs while Avoiding Liver and Spleen through Adsorption on Red Blood Cells|journal=ACS Nano|date=23 December 2013|volume=7|issue=12|pages=11129–11137|doi=10.1021/nn404853z|pmid=24182189|pmc=4128963}}</ref> Mitragotri's technologies are used to develop next generation therapies against diabetes, cancer, psoriasis, hemorrhage, trauma and infections.

Mitragotri has published over 400 research publications and is an inventor on over 300 patents/applications. His publications are cited over 81000 times with an h-index of 140.<ref>{{cite web|title=Samir Mitragotri|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=3_77zesAAAAJ&hl=en|publisher=Google Scholar|accessdate=14 May 2020}}</ref> Mitragotri is a member of the US [https://nam.edu/ National Academy of Medicine] and the US [[National Academy of Inventors]]. He is also a member of the US [[National Academy of Engineering]] since 2015 for the development, clinical translation, and commercialization of transdermal drug delivery systems. He is also an elected member of [https://twas.org/ The World Academy of Science], [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences|American Academy of Arts & Sciences]] and [[Indian National Academy of Engineering]]. He is a co-founder of several companies that are developing products based on his inventions. He received his PhD in [[chemical engineering]] at [[MIT]] and BS in chemical engineering from the [[Institute of Chemical Technology]]. Mitragotri serves on the editorial boards of several journals and has served as the founding editor-in-chief of ''Bioengineering and Translational Medicine''.
